title: rbac-v2-kms-region-pinning-audit-hardening
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Harden RBAC v2 to enforce KMS region pinning and emit audit logs for KMS residency decisions. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: Customers operating in regulated environments require deterministic KMS residency and stronger audit trails when RBAC v2 policies allow KMS key usage across regions. This change hardens RBAC v2 so that KMS region pinning is enforced by policy evaluation and all decisions are recorded in the audit log with tenancy and request context. Summary: - Add policy predicate and enforcement for kms.region_pinning on resources that reference customer-managed KMS keys. - Emit structured audit events whenever a policy allows, denies, or falls back for KMS region routing decisions. - Add integration hooks to the KMS client so runtime routing respects policy-residency constraints and surfaces why a request was routed or rejected. - Update docs and migration notes for operators to opt into enforcement via a feature flag before rollout. Checklist: - [x] New policy predicate implementation and unit tests - [x] Audit event schema and logging plumbing - [x] KMS client integration + fallback behavior tests - [x] End-to-end test in redwood-private installer with region pinning flag - [x] Documentation and release note Draft Implementation details: The change introduces a new policy predicate kms_region_allowed(resource.kms_key_arn, request.region) that returns allow/deny/needs_migration states. Policy evaluation is now consulted by the KMS routing layer in the serving runtime; when the predicate returns deny, the request is rejected with status 403 and a structured audit event is emitted (audit.action = "kms_region_pin_check", detail.reason = "policy_denied"). When the predicate returns needs_migration (existing resources with unspecified residency), the system records the event and defaults to audit-only mode when the feature-flag enforcement.rbac_v2.kms_region_pinning is set to "audit" (default during rollout). When the flag is "enforce", needs_migration behaves like deny. Audit events include: request id, actor, resource arn, evaluated policy id, location hint, and the exact predicate outcome to support compliance reviews. Files changed (high level): rbac/policies/kms_region_predicate.go -- predicate and evaluator logic rbac/policies/kms_region_predicate_test.go -- unit tests rbac/policy_engine/engine.go -- hook to surface predicate reasons to callers observability/audit/events.go -- new structured event type observability/audit/logger.go -- emit events with tracing context infra/kms/kms_client.go -- consults policy evaluation before selecting region infra/kms/kms_client_integration_test.go -- e2e routing tests docs/security/rbac-v2-kms-region-pinning.md -- migration and operator notes helm/redwood-private/values.yaml -- feature flag default set to "audit" Test plan: - Unit tests for predicate and engine integration (ci) - Integration tests exercising allow/deny/needs_migration flows against a mocked KMS routing table - E2E in redwood-private (installer) with a small cluster and two region backends - CI runs green on branch, manual security review sign-off requested from reviewers Rollout plan: 1) Merge in audit-only mode (feature flag default = "audit") 2) Monitor audit metrics and run a 48h canary (metric: kms_region_pin_check.denied_count, kms_region_pin_check.audit_count, and any production 403s) 3) If no regressions and acceptable false positives, flip to "enforce" for 10% of traffic and gradually increase to 100% 4) Provide operator migration guide to update resources with explicit residency tag if needed Rollback: Feature flag flip back to "audit" is immediate. For operator mistakes, an admin tool is provided to bulk-tag resources with residency and an emergency bypass metric is available for SRE. Related: ENG-4123 (policy predicate design), SEC-208 (security review), previous PRs: pr-314159-security-rbac-v2-kms-region-pinning-audit-enhancements, pr-272234-rbac-v2-kms-residency-audit-hardening Notes: This PR intentionally keeps enforcement gated behind a feature flag to observe real-world noise and adjust policy rules before hard enforcement. The audit schema is backwards compatible with our existing audit ingestion pipeline and uses a new event type so alerts can be configured independently.
